eyebrow: The T-SQL Development Course · Chapter Two
subtitle: Lesson 13 · Writing Data

eyebrow: From literal VALUES to a query
code:
INSERT INTO dbo.LessonDemo (ProductName, ListPrice, Color)
SELECT Name, ListPrice, Color
FROM Production.Product
WHERE ProductLine = 'R';
caption: No VALUES at all -- the SELECT's result set IS the source of the rows.

code:
INSERT INTO dbo.LessonDemo (ProductName, ListPrice, Color)
SELECT p.Name, p.ListPrice, p.Color
FROM Production.Product AS p
WHERE p.Color = 'Red';
caption: p.Name -> ProductName, p.ListPrice -> ListPrice -- names don't need to match.

eyebrow: Filter, sort, and limit before inserting
code:
INSERT INTO dbo.LessonDemo (ProductName, ListPrice, Color)
SELECT TOP (5) Name, ListPrice, Color
FROM Production.Product
WHERE Color IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY ListPrice DESC;
caption: Only the 5 priciest colored products land in dbo.LessonDemo.

eyebrow: One statement, any number of rows
code:
INSERT INTO dbo.LessonDemo (ProductName, ListPrice, Color)
SELECT Name, ListPrice, Color
FROM Production.Product
WHERE ListPrice BETWEEN 500 AND 1000;
caption: A single set-based copy -- whether the SELECT returns 3 rows or 3,000.
